papers.authors: Shashank Shekhar, Khushboo Bhagat, Aditya K. Padhi
papers.title: Structural rewiring of the mannose-binding pocket reveals adaptive FimH mutations that enhance uroplakin-associated glycan recognition and uropathogenic adhesion
papers.annotation: Integrative structural modeling, interface-based protein redesign, and mutational energy profiling of FimH-glycan-UPK interactions across human and porcine uroplakin contexts; identifies affinity-modulating substitutions including N135S, Y137F, D54G and D47V.

papers.authors: Aditya K. Padhi, Timir Tripathi
papers.title: A comprehensive protein design protocol to identify resistance mutations and signatures of adaptation in pathogens
papers.annotation: Describes a high-throughput computational protein design protocol for identifying hotspot residues, resistance mutations and signatures of adaptation in pathogen proteins.

papers.authors: Maximilian M. Sauer, Roman P. Jakob, Jonathan Eras, Sefer Baday, Deniz Eriş, Giulio Navarra, Simon Bernèche, Beat Ernst, Timm Maier, Rudi Glockshuber
papers.title: Catch-bond mechanism of the bacterial adhesin FimH
papers.annotation: Defines the force-dependent conformational mechanism of FimH catch-bond formation using crystal structures, kinetic analysis and molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.authors: Adinda Wellens, Corinne Garofalo, Hien Nguyen, Nani Van Gerven, Rikard Slättegård, Jean-Pierre Hernalsteens, Lode Wyns, Stefan Oscarson, Henri De Greve, Scott Hultgren, Julie Bouckaert
papers.title: Intervening with Urinary Tract Infections Using Anti-Adhesives Based on the Crystal Structure of the FimH–Oligomannose-3 Complex
papers.annotation: Provides the FimH–oligomannose-3 structural basis for anti-adhesive design and discusses blocking UPEC adhesion, invasion and intracellular persistence.

papers.authors: Haruaki Yanagisawa, Yoshihiro Kita, Toshiyuki Oda, Masahide Kikkawa
papers.title: Cryo-EM elucidates the uroplakin complex structure within liquid-crystalline lipids in the porcine urothelial membrane
papers.annotation: Provides a cryo-EM structural scaffold for the porcine uroplakin complex in a membrane context.

papers.authors: G Zhou, W J Mo, P Sebbel, G Min, T A Neubert, R Glockshuber, X R Wu, T T Sun, X P Kong
papers.title: Uroplakin Ia is the urothelial receptor for uropathogenic Escherichia coli: evidence from in vitro FimH binding
papers.annotation: Foundational receptor study demonstrating the role of uroplakin Ia in FimH-mediated attachment of UPEC to the urothelial surface.

papers.authors: Sheryl S. Justice, Chia Hung, et al.
papers.title: Differentiation and developmental pathways of uropathogenic Escherichia coli in urinary tract pathogenesis
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
papers.annotation: Defines the intracellular bacterial community developmental program underlying UPEC persistence and recurrence.

papers.authors: Zhilin Zeng, Juan Zhan, Kaimin Zhang, Huilong Chen, Sheng Cheng
papers.title: Global, regional, and national burden of urinary tract infections from 1990 to 2019: an analysis of the global burden of disease study 2019
papers.annotation: Provides the epidemiological basis for global, regional and national UTI burden estimates using Global Burden of Disease 2019 data.

papers.authors: Capitani G, Eidam O, Glockshuber R, Grütter MG
papers.title: Structural and functional insights into the assembly of type 1 pili from Escherichia coli
papers.annotation: Review of type 1 pilus biogenesis covering the donor-strand complementation/exchange mechanism, FimC as a protein-folding catalyst that accelerates subunit folding over 100-fold, and the FimD N-terminal domain as a flexible 'cargo sensor' that discriminates chaperone-subunit complexes via its disordered N-terminal tail.

papers.authors: Qin J, Wilson KA, Sarkar S, Heras B, O'Mara ML, Totsika M
papers.title: Conserved FimH mutations in the global Escherichia coli ST131 multi-drug resistant lineage weaken interdomain interactions and alter adhesin function
papers.annotation: MD simulations plus isogenic ST131 EC958 allelic-exchange assays showing that the R166H mutation in FimH30 (Clade C) weakens lectin-pilin interdomain hydrogen bonds, enriches pre-existing relaxed high-affinity conformations, and confers enhanced intestinal adhesion, bladder invasion and biofilm formation.

papers.authors: Lüthje P, Brauner A
papers.title: Virulence Factors of Uropathogenic E. coli and Their Interaction with the Host
papers.annotation: Comprehensive review of UPEC virulence and fitness factors: type 1/P/curli/Afa-Dr/S/F1C fimbriae, toxins (α-haemolysin, CNF1, SPATEs), iron-acquisition systems (siderophores, ChuA/Hma), and immune-evasion strategies including immune suppression, serum resistance and biofilm/IBC formation.

papers.authors: Dhakal BK, Kulesus RR, Mulvey MA
papers.title: Mechanisms and consequences of bladder cell invasion by uropathogenic Escherichia coli
papers.annotation: Review establishing UPEC as an opportunistic intracellular pathogen: FimH-mediated invasion via α3β1 integrins, lipid rafts and uroplakin zippering; IBC development in superficial facet cells; efflux via cAMP; quiescent intracellular reservoirs; and Afa/Dr-mediated, microtubule-dependent invasion routes.

papers.authors: Feenstra T, Thøgersen MS, Wieser E, Peschel A, Ball MJ, Brandes R, Satchell SC, Stockner T, Aarestrup FM, Rees AJ, Kain R
papers.title: Adhesion of Escherichia coli under flow conditions reveals potential novel effects of FimH mutations
papers.journal: European Journal of Clinical Microbiology & Infectious Diseases
papers.annotation: A 12-alanine-scan mutagenesis panel of the FimH mannose-binding pocket tested under physiological shear stress on endothelial biochips; identifies E50 and T53 as residues dispensable in static assays but crucial for adhesion under flow, highlighting assay-dependent phenotypes of FimH mutants.

papers.authors: Kątnik-Prastowska I, Lis J, Matejuk A
papers.title: Glycosylation of uroplakins. Implications for bladder physiopathology
papers.annotation: Review of uroplakin structure, assembly into the asymmetric unit membrane and differentiation-dependent glycosylation; UPIa carries high-mannose N-glycans (Asn169) that serve as the FimH receptor, whereas UPIb carries complex fucosylated glycans; covers UPIa/b, pro-UPII maturation, UPIII signalling and glycosylation changes in UTI, IC and cancer.

papers.authors: Neamati F, Moniri R, Khorshidi A, Saffari M
papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterization of the FimH Adhesin of Uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Its Novel Applications
papers.annotation: Review covering FimH two-domain architecture, the tyrosine gate, low/high-affinity conformational switching and catch-bond mechanics, pathoadaptive mutations, FimH-based molecular typing of UPEC, and therapeutic applications including mannosides, pilicides, anti-FimH vaccines and FimH display/adjuvant systems.

papers.authors: Busch A, Phan G, Waksman G
papers.title: Molecular mechanism of bacterial type 1 and P pili assembly
papers.journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A
papers.annotation: Review integrating structural, kinetic and thermodynamic data on chaperone-usher pilus assembly: donor-strand complementation and zip-in/zip-out exchange, usher NTD/CTD handover and gating, FimD-FimC-FimF-FimG-FimH tip assembly snapshots, and pilicide design targeting chaperone-usher interactions.

papers.authors: Matuszewski MA, Tupikowski K, Dołowy Ł, Szymańska B, Dembowski J, Zdrojowy R
papers.title: Uroplakins and their potential applications in urology
papers.annotation: Clinical review of uroplakin biology and applications: UPIa high-mannose glycans as the FimH-binding entry point for UPEC, IBC-linked recurrent UTI, uroplakins as specific diagnostic markers for urothelial cancer (tissue, urine ELISA, blood), urine UPIII mRNA as a potential VUR screening test, and uroplakin involvement in interstitial cystitis.

papers.authors: Schembri MA, Sokurenko EV, Klemm P
papers.title: Functional Flexibility of the FimH Adhesin: Insights from a Random Mutant Library
papers.annotation: Error-prone PCR mutant library of the FimH receptor-binding domain showing monomannose binding is highly mutation-sensitive while oligomannose binding is conserved; identifies P49 as critical, A25P as an oligomannose-enhancing variant, and demonstrates that pathoadaptive-like phenotypes arise readily outside the binding pocket via conformational effects.

papers.authors: Rabbani S, Krammer EM, Roos G, Zalewski A, Preston R, Eid S, Zihlmann P, Prévost M, Lensink MF, Thompson A, Ernst B, Bouckaert J
papers.title: Mutation of Tyr137 of the universal Escherichia coli fimbrial adhesin FimH relaxes the tyrosine gate prior to mannose binding
papers.annotation: Crystal structures, ITC, QM calculations and MD of Y48A/Y137A tyrosine-gate mutants show Tyr137 maintains backbone strain that is released upon ligand binding; the Y137A mutation prematurely relaxes the gate, uncouples Tyr48-Ile52 dynamics, collapses affinity for alkyl/aryl mannosides and exposes an adjacent EDTA-binding surface pocket.

papers.authors: Whelan S, Lucey B, Finn K
papers.title: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)-Associated Urinary Tract Infections: The Molecular Basis for Challenges to Effective Treatment
papers.annotation: Broad review of UPEC pathogenesis and treatment challenges: adhesin systems (type 1, P, S, Afa/Dr, TosA), curli and biofilm regulation, toxin and iron-acquisition virulence factors, chromosomal/enzymatic/efflux antibiotic-resistance mechanisms, the role of plasmids, integrons and insertion sequences, and alternatives such as vaccines, phage therapy, antipathogenic agents and nano-formulations.

papers.authors: Mysorekar IU, Hultgren SJ
papers.title: Mechanisms of uropathogenic Escherichia coli persistence and eradication from the urinary tract
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
papers.annotation: Mouse UTI model demonstrating quiescent intracellular reservoirs (QIRs) of UPEC in Lamp1-positive endosomes persisting up to 12 weeks; protamine-sulfate exfoliation eradicates superficial facet-cell QIRs but reactivation from underlying transitional-cell QIRs upon epithelial turnover seeds recurrent bacteriuria.

papers.authors: Waksman G, Hultgren SJ
papers.title: Structural biology of the chaperone-usher pathway of pilus biogenesis
papers.annotation: Landmark review of chaperone-usher structural biology: donor-strand complementation/exchange via P1-P5 pockets, zip-in zip-out exchange initiated at the P5 pocket, usher dimer function and subunit handover, adhesin-receptor structures (FimH-mannose, PapG-globoside), and anti-adhesive therapeutic strategies including pilicides and mannosides.

papers.authors: Nasi GI, Georgakopoulou KI, Theodoropoulou MK, Papandreou NC, Chrysina ED, Tsiolaki PL, Iconomidou VA
papers.title: Bacterial Lectin FimH and Its Aggregation Hot-Spots: An Alternative Strategy against Uropathogenic Escherichia coli
papers.annotation: Computational prediction (AMYLPRED2) of aggregation-prone regions in FimH followed by peptide synthesis, TEM/X-ray/FT-IR/Congo Red amyloid characterization and MD docking; peptide 125LIAVLILRQT134 self-assembles into amyloid-like fibrils, binds the FimH mannose pocket displacing mannose, and is unique to the E. coli proteome, proposing an anti-folding/anti-adhesion therapeutic strategy.

papers.authors: Schwartz DJ, Kalas V, Pinkner JS, Chen SL, Spaulding CN, Dodson KW, Hultgren SJ
papers.title: Positively selected FimH residues enhance virulence during urinary tract infection by altering FimH conformation
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
papers.annotation: fimH allelic swaps in UTI89 and CFT073 show positively selected residues 27/62/163 tune the elongated-versus-compact conformational equilibrium of FimH in the pilus tip; intermediate-affinity alleles outcompete high-affinity-locked or low-affinity variants during chronic cystitis, demonstrating that conformational switching, not maximal affinity, drives virulence.

papers.authors: Sauer MM, Jakob RP, Luber T, Canonica F, Navarra G, Ernst B, Unverzagt C, Maier T, Glockshuber R
papers.title: Binding of the Bacterial Adhesin FimH to Its Natural, Multivalent High-Mannose Type Glycan Targets
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.annotation: Kinetic and structural dissection of FimH binding to natural α2/α3/α6-linked dimannosides: the S-state binds ~2000-fold tighter than the A-state via ~70,000-fold slower dissociation consistent with a ligand-shifted domain-separation thermodynamic cycle; analytical gel filtration shows up to three FimH molecules bind one N-glycan with negative cooperativity imposed by the chitobiose core.

papers.authors: Sokurenko E
papers.title: Pathoadaptive Mutations in Uropathogenic Escherichia coli
papers.annotation: Eco-evo review of UPEC pathoadaptation contrasting horizontal gene transfer with gene inactivation, amplification and variation; catalogs mutator phenotypes, LPS/flagellum loss, FimH/DraE/PapG adhesin hotspot mutations under positive selection, genome-wide screens of core genes under selection, and strategies to detect pathoadaptive mutations in clinical isolates.
